hints: At a constant speed on a horizontal road, the driving force equals the resisting force ($F_D = 1550\text{ N}$).
Apply the power equation $P = F_D \times v$ with $v = 40\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and convert the answer from watts to kilowatts.
walkthrough:
The car is traveling on a horizontal road at constant speed ($a = 0$), so the driving force of the engine balances the resistance force:
$$F_D = F_{\text{resistance}} = 1550\text{ N}$$

The formula relating power, driving force, and velocity is:
$$P = F_D \times v$$

Substitute the driving force $F_D = 1550\text{ N}$ and speed $v = 40\text{ m s}^{-1}$ into the formula:
$$P = 1550 \times 40 = 62000\text{ W}$$

Convert the power from watts to kilowatts by dividing by $1000$:
$$P = \frac{62000}{1000} = 62\text{ kW}$$

hints: Calculate the new reduced power by subtracting $22\text{ kW}$ from $62\text{ kW}$.
Find the instantaneous driving force from $F_{\text{new}} = \frac{P_{\text{new}}}{v}$ while the speed is still $40\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Apply Newton's second law in the direction of motion: $F_{\text{new}} - F_{\text{res}} = ma$, and state the deceleration.
walkthrough:
First, calculate the new reduced power of the engine. The power is suddenly decreased by $22\text{ kW}$ from $62\text{ kW}$:
$$P_{\text{new}} = 62000 - 22000 = 40000\text{ W}$$

Immediately after the power change, the car's speed is still $v = 40\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Use $P = Fv$ to find the new driving force $F_{\text{new}}$:
$$F_{\text{new}} = \frac{P_{\text{new}}}{v} = \frac{40000}{40} = 1000\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law in the forward direction of motion: $\sum F = ma$:
$$F_{\text{new}} - F_{\text{resistance}} = ma$$

Substitute $F_{\text{new}} = 1000\text{ N}$, $F_{\text{resistance}} = 1550\text{ N}$, and mass $m = 1100\text{ kg}$:
$$1000 - 1550 = 1100a$$
$$-550 = 1100a$$

Divide both sides by $1100$ to find the acceleration:
$$a = \frac{-550}{1100} = -0.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

A negative acceleration indicates deceleration. State the magnitude as the deceleration:
$$\text{Deceleration} = 0.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

hints: At constant speed, acceleration is zero, so the driving force $F_D$ must balance both the component of weight down the slope and the resistance force.
Calculate the weight component down the $8^\circ$ slope: $W_\parallel = mg\sin 8^\circ = 1100(10)\sin 8^\circ$.
Find total resistance $F_D = mg\sin 8^\circ + 1550$, then use $P = F_D \times v$ with power $80\text{ kW} = 80000\text{ W}$ to solve for $v$.
walkthrough:
When a vehicle moves up an inclined slope at constant speed, its acceleration is zero ($a = 0$). By Newton's first law, the forward driving force $F_D$ equals the total backward forces:
$$F_D = mg\sin\theta + F_{\text{resistance}}$$

Substitute the given mass $m = 1100\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, angle $\theta = 8^\circ$, and resistance $F_{\text{resistance}} = 1550\text{ N}$:
$$F_D = 1100 \times 10 \times \sin 8^\circ + 1550 = 11000\sin 8^\circ + 1550$$

Calculate the numerical value of the driving force:
$$11000 \times 0.139173 + 1550 = 1530.9 + 1550 = 3080.9\text{ N}$$

Now relate the driving force to engine power using the formula $P = F_D \times v$:
$$P = F_D v$$

Substitute power $P = 80\text{ kW} = 80000\text{ W}$ and $F_D = 3080.9\text{ N}$:
$$80000 = 3080.9 v$$

Divide both sides by $3080.9$ to isolate $v$:
$$v = \frac{80000}{3080.9} \approx 25.966\text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 26.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
